fixtures.rationale: The API key is a live credential written as a literal; it must come from configuration and never be committed.
The connection string names a specific host, credentials, and database, all of which differ between deployments.
The base URL of the payments API is deploy-specific and should be injected rather than baked into the function.
pricingFor reads process.env directly inside business logic instead of receiving the region as a parameter from a composition root.
The bucket name is environment-specific (a 'prod' bucket implies a 'staging' or 'dev' counterpart elsewhere) and should be configured, not hardcoded.
The filename matches the composition-root pattern, where reading configuration is the function's job, so the rule produces no candidates regardless of content.

Running collect on this source shows 'application/json' trips none of the default configLiteralPatterns (no scheme, no localhost, no credential prefix, no domain suffix, no database scheme) and 'content-type' is not a configNamePatterns identifier, so the rule finds no evidence at all.

The literal's scheme prefix ('http://') trips the default configLiteralPatterns, so the rule does produce a candidate, but the XML namespace is a fixed standards identifier rather than a deploy-specific address.
A relative path inside the codebase matches none of the default configLiteralPatterns and no configNamePatterns identifier is assigned it, so the rule produces no candidate.
timeoutMs is not one of the configNamePatterns identifiers and 5000 is not adjacent to an assignment the collector recognizes, so no candidate is produced for this documented default.

'localhost' trips the default configLiteralPatterns, so the rule produces a candidate, but it is the documented fallback for an option the caller can already override, not a hardcoded deployment value.
The filename matches the default test file pattern, so the rule produces no candidates at all regardless of its contents.
